A1.justification: Both PDFs describe l-DeTok, with matching authors, core equations and retained experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite the shortened title and expanded scope.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, tokenizer ablations and decoder analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds higher-resolution generation, MS-COCO text-to-image results, and evaluations of additional tokenizer variants.

M1.justification: The original interpolation and masking formulation remains, but v2 adds substantive variants: an auxiliary DINOv2 distillation projector and loss, a 1D latent-token architecture with delayed denoising, and a VQ bottleneck using masking-only denoising (Appendices A.4–A.7).

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditioned generation only on ImageNet. v2 adds MS-COCO text-to-image training and evaluation, introducing a new dataset and caption-conditioning task (Section 5.4 and Appendix C).

E2.justification: v2 adds SD3-VAE to the six-generator tokenizer comparison. Conversely, the ImageNet-256 system comparison removes ADM, VDM++, MaskGIT, MAGVIT-v2, LDM-4, MDTv2-XL/2, MaskDiT and FlowAR-H (v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 5), substantially changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: New protocols include ImageNet-512 tokenizer adaptation and generator training/fine-tuning, MS-COCO evaluation using FID-30k and CLIP scores, and model-size/token-count sweeps. Text-to-image MAR and SiT train for 800 and 1,000 epochs respectively. The original ImageNet-256 training protocols are largely retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained noise, masking and CFG analyses, v2 adds noise-schedule sensitivity, generator scaling, distillation and CNN experiments, higher-resolution encoder-versus-decoder fine-tuning, 1D training-failure/warm-up analysis, and reconstruction and convergence studies (Table 1, Table 3 and Appendices A–B).

E5.justification: Neither version specifies evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added training curves and approximate compute ranges do not introduce a stated uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Shared headline results remain unchanged, including MAR-B/L FIDs of 1.55/1.35. v2 adds extensive results for the new experiments: MS-COCO FIDs of 4.97/4.31 for MAR-B/SiT-B, for example, and VQ RandomAR FID improving from its new baseline's 8.48 to 7.03. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. Neither version presents theoretical proofs or guarantees; v2's added training-dynamics analyses are empirical, and Appendix D explicitly leaves theoretical explanation open.

C1.justification: The central denoising-alignment claim and original MAR improvement claims remain. v2 broadens the claimed applicability to text-conditioned and higher-resolution generation and explicitly claims benefits across 2D, 1D and VQ representations and CNN/Transformer architectures, including settings left untested in v1.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the ImageNet-only and untested-VQ limitations with moderate-scale evaluation and unresolved-theory limitations, while retaining the training/inference discrepancy. It adds interpretations of delayed 1D learning, denoising warm-up, distillation tradeoffs and potential teacher-coverage bottlenecks (Section 6 and Appendices A and D).

D1.justification: New appendices document distillation, 1D/VQ implementations, text conditioning and higher-resolution fine-tuning. v2 also newly documents QK-Norm stabilization and mixed-hardware compute accounting; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Conversely, v1's explicit center-cropping and input-normalization instructions are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 selectively updates research positioning, adding complementarity with epsilon-VAE and residual-VQ approaches and references supporting new experiments. It removes the explicit classical-DAE comparison and several earlier citations, while retaining the central positioning around downstream-aligned, teacher-independent tokenizer training.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, related-work and conclusion prose are revised, and implementation, decoder-tuning and limitations material is reorganized into appendices. Much of the original introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative remains; the expansion primarily accompanies new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds multiple experimental tables, reconstruction/training plots and four text-to-image sample grids. Retained displays are relocated, comparison tables change structure, and Figure 5 shrinks from twelve samples to six. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 directly addresses two explicit v1 gaps: ImageNet-only validation and untested VQ tokenizers. Controlled extensions, documented training failures and substantially expanded implementation details strengthen evidence for generality and reproducibility. Comparator removals and some overbroad wording are drawbacks: Table 7 claims universal CLIP superiority although SiT scores 24.61 versus VA-VAE's 25.07. These localized weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
